editorial.headline: Cultivating Prohibited Plants: Closed to Foreign Investment
editorial.standfirst: This integrated cultivation category is open across four enterprise scales, yet is closed to PMA nationally and blocked for foreign registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity covers the cultivation of narcotic plants and prohibited medicinal plants. Its stated scope takes in the full agricultural chain: land preparation, planting, crop maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest work when these are carried out as one continuous sequence. That last qualification matters. The activity is framed as an integrated operation, joining work in the ground with the follow-on handling that belongs to the same run of activity. It is therefore not merely a label for planting; it describes the connected agricultural process set out in the record.

The category is available to businesses at every listed enterprise scale: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. The practical registrant is accordingly a business undertaking that full cultivation-and-post-harvest sequence, at any of those stated scales. Scale availability, however, answers only the size question. It should not be confused with the foreign-investment position. The record places enterprise scale and foreign ownership in separate fields, and they lead to different conclusions: all four scales are listed as open, while PMA is not.

Nationally, the foreign-investment status is TERTUTUP, with a maximum foreign ownership figure of 0%. The implication is direct: this activity is closed to PMA registration at national level. There is no partial foreign stake within the stated ceiling; the ceiling itself is zero. For an investor assessing an Indonesian structure, that is the point on which the entry question turns. The availability of Micro through Large scales does not create a foreign-investment route, because the national ownership position remains closed.

Bali reaches the same result, rather than offering a regional opening. Its status is TERTUTUP, the record marks it as blocked for PMA, and the stated reason identifies the national closure and 0% position. Accordingly, a foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today. The Bali record also cites a provincial rule that blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI from PMA across the island on a permanent basis. That provincial setting is relevant context for Bali registration, but the conclusion here is already unambiguous: national closure and Bali's recorded blocked status point in one direction. This is an activity whose listed business scales remain available, while foreign ownership does not.
